name: Gedaliah
overview: Gedaliah, appointed governor by the king of Babylon after the Jewish captivity, played a pivotal role in caring for the remnant of Judah, as Jeremiah was entrusted to his care and lived among the people under his leadership (Jeremiah 39:14; 40:5-6). He received warnings about a conspiracy against him from Johanan and the military captains, highlighting the volatile environment in which he governed (Jeremiah 40:13). His leadership was tragically cut short when he was killed by Ishmael, underscoring the challenges faced by God's people during this period of exile and transition.
